questions.q: What does a table-level ACL actually control?
options: Access to one specific field on a table
Access to a record as a whole, for one specific operation
Only whether a UI policy can run on the form
The order fields appear on a form layout
questions.explain: A table-level ACL is a single gate for an entire operation (read, write, create, delete) on records of that table, without caring about individual fields.

questions.q: How is a field-level ACL named, following ServiceNow's real convention?
options: <table>.<operation>, the same as a table-level ACL
<operation>.<table>
<table>.<field>, such as incident.caller_id
field_level_<table>_<field>
questions.explain: Table-level ACLs use <table>.<operation> (like incident.read); field-level ACLs use <table>.<field> (like incident.caller_id).

questions.q: A user passes incident.read but a specific field is blank on the form. What does this most likely mean?
options: The table-level ACL is broken and needs to be rebuilt
A field-level ACL on that field failed, independent of the passing table-level ACL
This is impossible if the table-level read ACL passed
The user's role was deleted mid-session
questions.explain: Field-level ACLs are checked in addition to the table-level ACL — passing the table-level check does not guarantee access to every field.

questions.q: In the lesson's contractor example, why can a contractor update an Incident's work notes but not see the Caller field?
options: incident.write and incident.caller_id are two independent ACLs, and only one of them lists the contractor role
The Caller field doesn't exist on the Incident table
Contractors are blocked from the Incident table entirely
Field-level ACLs only apply to the create operation
questions.explain: incident.write (table-level) allows the contractor role; incident.caller_id (field-level) requires itil instead — two separate, independently evaluated ACLs.

questions.q: Why is it useful to recognize an ACL's name pattern at a glance?
options: It tells you immediately whether you're looking at a table-level or field-level rule without opening the record
ACL names have no functional meaning in ServiceNow
Only field-level ACLs have names; table-level ACLs are unnamed
The name determines which database the ACL is stored in
questions.explain: <table>.<operation> versus <table>.<field> is a visual cue in the Access Control list for which layer you're reading.
